What Are Sandblasting Services?

Sandblasting services use compressed air to drive abrasive media against metal, removing rust, scale and old surface debris. The result is clean, bare metal with an even texture that lets powder coating grip firmly and last for years, even in tough outdoor conditions.

The word sandblasting is common, but most modern work uses other abrasives, so the broader names are media blasting and abrasive blasting. Each media cuts differently. Aluminum oxide blasting and steel grit blasting cut fast and leave a rougher surface, while glass bead blasting leaves a smoother, cleaner finish. The texture left behind is called the surface profile, or anchor profile, and it gives powder something to hold. Good blast cleaning removes everything that would stop a coating from bonding and leaves a bare metal finish ready to coat.

That is why we treat industrial sandblasting as part of the coating process, not a separate chore. Sandblasting and powder coating work best when one team plans both, because clean steel starts to show flash rust soon after blasting. Skipping this link in the chain is the most common reason a coating fails early.
How Does Our Sandblasting Process Work?

Our sandblasting services follow five stages: inspection, blast media selection, blasting, cleanup, and handoff to coating. Each stage protects the metal and the finish, and blasted parts move to coating quickly so rust never gets a chance to return to the metal before the coating goes on.

items: Inspection and planning (on arrival). We check each part for heavy rust, pitted and scaled steel, weld spatter and thin sections. We then decide whether the job suits our shop or on-site sandblasting. Early inspection lets us flag problem areas before they cost you time.

Blast media selection. The right media depends on the metal and the finish you need. Tough rust and scale call for harder media, while softer metals and cosmetic parts need gentler options. We confirm the choice with you when the finish or tolerance is critical.

Blasting. Our operators work across every surface, including welds, corners and recesses. They adjust pressure and distance so rust and mill-scale removal is complete without damaging thin sections. Industrial sandblasting at this stage is methodical, never rushed.
Cleanup. Compressed air and brushing clear spent media and dust from holes, seams and enclosed sections. Trapped grit would cause defects under the powder, so we never skip this step.
Inspection and handoff. We confirm a uniform, blast-cleaned surface, then move the part toward coating as soon as possible, since flash rust can form quickly on clean steel.

blocks.text: Timing matters as much as technique. Shop blasting sits inside our standard 48-hour turnaround, and we receive parts Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM. For mobile sandblasting, tell us the site, access and schedule when you request a quote and we will plan the visit around your deadline. Industrial sandblasting is scheduled alongside coating, so a blasted part never waits long between steps. That planning prevents the gaps that let bare metal rust, and it keeps your project moving.
Which Metals and Parts Need Sandblasting?

Steel and iron benefit most, because rust and scale form naturally on them. Cast parts, structural steel, fabricated frames and heavy equipment also respond well. Thin or soft metals need gentler media, so our sandblasting services plan the method for each metal before blasting starts.

items: Steel and iron. Sandblasting steel removes rust and mill scale, the hard grey layer left by hot rolling that blocks coating adhesion. It is the most common job we handle, and it suits everything from small brackets to large frames.
Welded and cast parts. Sandblasting weldments cleans weld discoloration and spatter, and gives rust removal from metal even in tight corners.
Aluminum and softer metals. Gentler media protects the surface, so we choose finer abrasives and lower pressure for these parts, which keeps edges and details sharp.

blocks.text: Typical work includes sandblasting structural steel, sandblasting gates and railings, sandblasting trailers and frames, machine bases and equipment housings. Sandblasting heavy equipment and sandblasting large fabrications can be done in our shop or on site, so confirm the part size when you request a quote. Whether you need sandblasting metal parts one at a time or industrial sandblasting for a full production run, we plan the abrasive blasting to protect the metal.
What Sandblasting Options Does Koojo Offer?

Koojo offers shop blasting for parts we can move, a mobile service for work on site, and a choice of blast media to suit the metal. Blasting is most often paired with powder coating, so ask us how your job should be planned from start to finish.

items: Shop sandblasting. Parts come to our Milton shop, where blasting happens in a controlled setting with dust containment and a fast route into coating.

Mobile sandblasting. Our mobile blasting crew brings on-site blasting equipment to structures, large frames and fixed equipment that are hard to move. Portable sandblasting equipment suits these jobs. Share site access and layout when you quote.
Media choices. Blast media selection covers aluminum oxide, steel grit and glass bead, matched to the metal and the finish you want. Larger industrial sandblasting jobs often use a mix of media.

What comes next. After blasting, many parts still need washing and masking, which our [powder coating surface preparation](/services/surface-preparation) service covers. Parts with aged coatings may suit our [restoration and recoating](/services/restoration-recoating) service.

blocks.text: Not sure which option fits? Send photos and the part material. We will recommend an approach, and our sandblasting services advice comes with your quote. Choosing the right method up front avoids a damaged part, and protects the rust protection your coating is meant to provide.
How Do We Check Blasting Quality?

We verify blasting through visual inspection and a surface check before coating. Koojo is certified through the Absolute Bureau of Certification, our inspection steps are documented, and test reports are available on request, so you can trust the work behind every finish.

Quality starts at intake, when we look for heavy rust, thick scale and old coatings. After blasting, a blast-cleaned surface should look even in colour, with no shiny rust patches, leftover scale or traces of old paint. Surface profile matters too. If the surface is too smooth, powder grips poorly, and if it is too rough, peaks can show through the finish and shorten its life. We check this before parts move on, and we flag any concern with you early.

Our sandblasting services are never signed off until the part passes these checks. Consistent industrial sandblasting also means the next batch matches the last, because we keep records that support repeat orders. Cleanup is part of quality. Loose grit left in seams spoils the coating, so we clear it before parts move on. Because clean bare steel can show flash rust quickly, we plan coating soon after blasting, and we hold shop and mobile work to the same documented checks every time. See our [certification](/certification) page for details on how we work. Careful abrasive blasting also leaves the clean bare steel that strong coatings need.

Which Industries Use Our Sandblasting Services?

Fabricators, contractors, farm and heavy equipment owners and manufacturers use us most. These customers need dependable industrial sandblasting, quick turnaround and a clean surface that supports coating. Our approach scales from single parts to production runs, with the same care every time.

See how we support [contractors and construction](/industries/contractors-construction) teams, who often need work done on site, and [agricultural and heavy equipment](/industries/agricultural-heavy-equipment) owners, where heavy rust is the main concern, so you can find the page that matches your work. Our sandblasting services also support our wider [industrial powder coating](/services/industrial-powder-coating) work and the full range of [powder coating services](/services) at our Milton shop.
Sandblasting FAQs

Short answer: sandblasting removes rust, scale and old debris to leave clean bare metal, and it can happen in our shop or on your site. These answers cover mobile work, terminology, timing and scheduling, so you know what to expect before you book.

blocks.a: Yes. We offer mobile sandblasting for work that cannot travel to our shop. Send site details, photos and your preferred schedule when you request a quote so we can plan access, cleanup and timing before anyone arrives.

blocks.q: What is the difference between sandblasting and abrasive blasting?
blocks.a: Sandblasting is the common name, while abrasive blasting is the broader term for any media driven by air. Most modern work uses media other than sand, chosen to suit the metal, the finish and the coating that follows.

blocks.q: How soon should blasted parts be coated?
blocks.a: As soon as possible. Clean steel develops flash rust quickly, so we plan blasting and coating together to keep the surface protected. Tell us your deadline and we will sequence the work to match.

blocks.q: How long does a sandblasting job take?
blocks.a: Shop work follows our standard 48-hour turnaround for typical orders. Large, heavily rusted or mobile jobs are scheduled when we quote, once we know the size, condition and access.
